entity: United States Department of Housing and Urban Development
stance_basis: states awareness of no significantly harmful effect from temporary 4(f) land use, and separately concurs with no adverse environmental impact on low-income neighborhoods
summary: The United States Department of Housing and Urban Development provided two distinct comments: one during early coordination (September 17, 1974) stating awareness of no significantly harmful effect from the temporary use of Section 4(f) land west of Thorn Creek Bridge, and one in response to the Draft Environmental Statement indicating no reason to believe the proposed action would have an adverse environmental impact on low-income neighborhoods. Both comments are supportive or non-objecting in nature, reflecting a neutral/non-opposing stance rather than active advocacy for or against the project.
complaint_summary: HUD, in response to the Draft Environmental Statement, stated that after coordinating with its Regional Office and affected community action agencies, it had no reason to believe the proposed action would have an adverse environmental impact on low-income neighborhoods.

statement.opening_anchor:
6. Department of Housing and Urban Development
This office in coordination with our Regional Office, and the affected community action agencies have carefully reviewed this statement.
statement.closing_anchor: On the basis of information from this review, we have no reason to believe that the proposed action will have an adverse environmental impact on the low income neighborhoods involved. Should we receive any further information we will advise.

summary_quote: We are aware of no significantly harmful effect that the temporary use of this 4(f) land west of Thorn Creek Bridge would have on this area.
